summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: almost every Hindi video gets 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly stays under 100 views. The best videos are the 'X doesn't see/hear, it only senses Y' myth-busting ones (robot falling without gyro, clap switch hearing noise not claps), which also earn the most likes, saves and shares. Generic 'How does X work?' titles about everyday places (lift, tap, mall door, smoke detector) get weak results on both platforms, and several videos have no Instagram numbers at all.
winningPattern: A single relatable gadget or hobby-robot (clap switch, gyro robot, IR robot, DHT11, mic) with a surprising 'it doesn't do what you think' hook in Hinglish, e.g. 'X ko Y nahi dikhta, sirf Z karta hai' or 'X ke bina Y turant gir jata'. Short, curiosity-driven titles with one emoji, posted mainly on Instagram Reels, where reach is ~1,000-1,200 per video. On YouTube only the clap switch and gyro robot did decently (400-680 views), so Maker-project topics with a visible demo beat explainer topics.
doMore: Use the 'doesn't X, only Y' myth-flip hook, naming the surprising real mechanism in the title
Make follow-ups to the winners: gyro/balancing robot, clap switch variants, line follower, IR robot obstacle avoidance
Show a physical demo (robot falling, clap triggering light) in the first 2 seconds
Post every video on both platforms; 8 videos have zero Instagram numbers, so cross-post them
Prompt saves and shares with a closing line like 'Save this for your next Arduino project'
stopDoing: Generic 'X Kaise Kaam Karta Hai? 🤔' titles for public-place gadgets (lift, tap, mall door, street light)
Repeating the same topic within days (3 smoke/IR/PIR/heat-sensor near-duplicates split the audience and dilute results)
Posting English-language videos on a Hindi channel without a plan, as the single English video got no Instagram traction
